anchor.quote: Fix a number $\beta$ of places, a positive integer, and lengths $\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_\beta$, each a positive integer.
Here $\lambda_j$ is the length of place $j$, the number of values its digit can take.
The place index $j$ runs from $1$ to $\beta$ and names a place
Let $\Lambda = \lambda_1\lambda_2\cdots\lambda_\beta$ be the product of the lengths, the number of distinct digit strings the system can write.
The place value of place $j$ is $w_j = \lambda_1\lambda_2\cdots\lambda_{j-1}$, the product of the lengths of the places below it, with $w_1 = 1$.
Let $\nu$ be an integer with $0 \le \nu < \Lambda$, the integer being written.
The digit $e_j$ at place $j$ is an integer with $0 \le e_j < \lambda_j$, the digit of the expansion at that place.
